Can someone tell me what RSS is and how it works?

Depending on who you ask, it stands for "Rich Site Syndication" or "Really Simple Syndication".

Essentially, an RSS feed is an XML document containing all of the content posted on the website in reverse chronological order (newest first).

The idea was (is?) that when a website posts new content, their RSS feed also shows that new content. The reader (you) will run a program that periodically checks the website in question, pull the feed and check to see if any new content is available.

That doesn't seem like a big deal. It is when it's used on 50 sites with irregular update schedules.

Pretty much the only use RSS gets nowadays is for podcasters. Podcast clients subscribe to RSS feeds, when a new episode is available, it automagically downloads the program and alerts you that you have new content.

When RSS feeds first came out, you could generally get the entire article in your feed, which removed the need to actually visit the site, you could just read the article in your feedreader. This was powerful. You could basically create your own newspaper of content you wanted to read, and it was all fetched into one place. Then there was Atom and there were different specs for RSS and not everybody offered a feed that your program would understand.

It kind of went to shit.

Then websites started truncating the post to get you to come to the site to read the full article, so they would still get the ad revenue. When that wasn't enough, many started including ads in their RSS feed itself.
